title: A generating sum of pulled-back sections has a generating summand downstairs
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $g:X\to Y$ a scheme morphism, and $M$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $\iota$ be any type, $s\subset\iota$ a finite set, $a:\iota\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $\sigma:\iota\to\Gamma(Y,M)$, and $y\in X$. Write $g^*\sigma_r\in\Gamma(X,g^*M)$ for the global pullback section, obtained from the pullback adjunction unit and restriction from $g^{-1}(Y)$ to the top open [def-pc-module-pullback, lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]. If $\sum_{r\in s} a_r\,g^*\sigma_r$ is a local free generator at $y$ [def-sc-local-free-generator, def-sc-section-generating-locus], then there exists $r\in s$ such that $\sigma_r$ is a local free generator at $g(y)$. There are no quasi-compactness, field, flatness, or nonempty-index hypotheses.

source.place: lines 77-113, exists_generatesAt_of_generatesAt_sum; local coefficient criterion (Stacks Modules Tag 01CY)

proof.text: Choose an open W containing g(y) and a free generator e of M on W, using invertibility. For every r, write the restriction of sigma r uniquely as f r times e. The pullback of e freely generates on g inverse W. Restricting the given sum to that open gives b times this pulled-back generator, where b is the sum over r in s of the restricted a r times g.app W (f r). These are the coefficient and pullback identities used in the existing Lean proof.

The local coefficient criterion for a free generator shows that generation of the sum at y puts y in the basic open D(b). The basic open of a finite sum is contained in the union of the basic opens of its summands; the basic open of each product is contained in D(g.app W (f r)). Thus some r in s satisfies y in D(g.app W (f r)). This also covers s empty: D(0) is empty, so the hypothesis is impossible.

The inverse-image identity for basic opens gives g(y) in D(f r). Apply the local coefficient criterion in the converse direction to sigma r restricted to W = f r times e. It follows that sigma r generates M at g(y); together with r in s this is the asserted witness. All steps are implemented in the attached existing, sorry-free theorem; no new Lean declaration is introduced.
